title: Install a new application
subtitle: Guided wizard: no YAML needed. Before applying you will see the summary, risks, cluster validation and generated YAML.
fixErrors: Fix the highlighted fields to continue.

name.explain: The name identifies the application in the cluster; the namespace is the "space" it is created in (for example production or test).
name.name: Application name
name.nameHint: Lowercase, digits and '-', max 50 characters. It becomes the Deployment, Service and Ingress name.
name.nsHint: Resources are created in this namespace.
name.createNs: Create the namespace if it does not exist
name.createNsHint: Select only for a new environment: the namespace is created together with the application.
name.createNsAdminOnly: Only an Administrator can create new namespaces.

image.explain: The image contains the application. Enter the repository without tag (the tag is chosen in the next step).
image.pullSecretHint: Name of a kubernetes.io/dockerconfigjson Secret in the namespace, required for private registries.
image.fromOnboarding: Values pre-filled by the image onboarding (image verified).
image.notVerified: Not sure the image exists or is accessible?
image.goOnboarding: Verify it with the onboarding wizard

tag.explain: The tag is the image version. Always use a precise version: it makes updates and rollbacks predictable.
tag.latestText: "latest" can change over time: different nodes may run different versions and a rollback does not guarantee the previous version.

replicas.explain: Replicas are identical copies of the application. Kubernetes keeps them running: if one fails it creates another.
replicas.zero: With 0 replicas the application is created but not started.
replicas.one: With 1 replica there is no redundancy: a failure, restart or update can cause a short outage.
replicas.many: {{count}} replicas: the service stays available even if one copy stops.

port.explain: The port the application listens on inside the container. It is used to create the Service and the health checks.
port.portHint: Leave empty if the application receives no traffic (e.g. a worker).
port.envHint: Non-secret configuration. Passwords and tokens do NOT go here: use a Secret.

cpu.explain: The request is the CPU reserved for the application: Kubernetes uses it to pick the node. The limit is the maximum usable: beyond it the application is throttled (not killed). 1 = one core, 250m = a quarter core.
cpu.limitHint: Optional. Without a limit the application can use free CPU of the node.

memory.explain: The request is the reserved memory; the limit is the maximum: if exceeded the application is killed (OOMKilled) and restarted. Mi = mebibyte, Gi = gibibyte.
memory.limitHint: Recommended: it protects the node from excessive usage.
memory.noLimit: Without a memory limit an application bug can exhaust the node memory and affect other applications too.

storage.explain: If the application must keep data (databases, uploaded files), it needs a persistent volume: without it data is lost when the Pod is recreated.

am.ReadWriteOnce: Read/write from one node at a time (the most common case).
am.ReadWriteMany: Read/write from many nodes (requires shared storage, e.g. NFS).

storage.rwoText: A ReadWriteOnce volume can be mounted by one node only: with {{replicas}} replicas some will stay stuck. Use 1 replica, ReadWriteMany or a StatefulSet.

net.explain: The Service gives the application a stable address; the Ingress publishes it externally with a domain name.

typeDesc.none: No network access (e.g. workers processing queues).
typeDesc.ClusterIP: Reachable only inside the cluster. The safest; use it with an Ingress for external access.
typeDesc.NodePort: Exposed on a port (30000-32767) of every node. Useful for tests, less controlled.
typeDesc.LoadBalancer: External address provided by the infrastructure (if available).

net.servicePortHint: Leave empty to use the container port ({{port}}).
net.ingressExplain: The Ingress forwards HTTP requests for a domain name to the Service.
net.tlsHint: kubernetes.io/tls Secret with certificate and key for HTTPS.

health.explain: Health checks let Kubernetes avoid sending traffic to copies not ready (readiness) and restart stuck copies (liveness).
health.noPort: Without a port HTTP/TCP checks are not available.
health.readinessExplain: Until it passes, the Pod receives no traffic. Essential for updates without outages.
health.livenessExplain: If it keeps failing, the container is restarted. Do not make it too aggressive.

summary.explain: This is what will be created. PKM validated the configuration directly on the cluster (dry-run): nothing has been applied yet.
summary.whatText: The application {{name}} will be started in namespace {{namespace}} with {{replicas}} replicas of image {{image}}.
summary.dryRunSkipped: Validation not run: fix the blocking problems first.

blocking.namespace_missing: Namespace {{namespace}} does not exist: pick it from the list or (Administrator) enable namespace creation.

zero_replicas.title: Zero replicas
zero_replicas.text: The application will not be started.

single_replica.title: Single replica
single_replica.text: No redundancy: failures and updates can cause outages.

latest_tag.title: latest tag
latest_tag.text: The actual version can change without notice; rollback is not reliable.

no_memory_limit.title: No memory limit
no_memory_limit.text: The application can use all the memory of the node.

no_requests.title: Requests not set
no_requests.text: Kubernetes cannot schedule the Pod properly; under pressure it is among the first evicted.

no_readiness.title: No readiness probe
no_readiness.text: Traffic can reach copies not ready yet, also during updates.

no_liveness.title: No liveness probe
no_liveness.text: An application that hangs without exiting will not be restarted automatically.

rwo_multi_replica.title: RWO volume with {{replicas}} replicas
rwo_multi_replica.text: Replicas beyond the first cannot mount the volume.

recreate_strategy.title: Updates with Recreate strategy
recreate_strategy.text: With a ReadWriteOnce volume old Pods are stopped before new ones start: short outage at every update.

nodeport_exposed.title: NodePort exposure
nodeport_exposed.text: The application is reachable on every node: check the firewall.

loadbalancer_exposed.title: LoadBalancer exposure
loadbalancer_exposed.text: The application gets an external address: check who can reach it.

ingress_no_tls.title: Ingress without TLS
ingress_no_tls.text: External traffic travels in clear text (HTTP).

secret_in_env.title: Possible secret in variables
secret_in_env.text: A variable named like PASSWORD/TOKEN contains a clear-text value: use a Secret.

overwrite_existing.title: Existing resources will be updated
overwrite_existing.text: They already exist: {{resources}}. Their configuration will be replaced.

deploy.explain: Press Deploy to create the resources of {{name}} in namespace {{namespace}}. The operation is recorded in the audit log.
deploy.previewInvalid: Validation failed: go back to the summary and fix the problems.
deploy.failedHint: Resources created successfully remain in the cluster. Fix the error and repeat the deploy: existing resources will be updated.
deploy.slowTitle: The start is taking longer than expected
deploy.slowText: Check the Operations Center and the Deployment events: typical causes are an image that cannot be pulled (ImagePullBackOff), insufficient resources (Pending) or startup errors (CrashLoopBackOff).

err.dnsLabel: Use lowercase, digits and '-', start and end with a letter or digit.
err.tagInImage: Put the tag in the Tag step, not in the image name.
err.cpuFormat: Invalid CPU value: use millicores (250m) or cores (0.5, 2).
err.memFormat: Invalid value: use Mi or Gi (e.g. 256Mi, 1Gi).
err.requestOverLimit: The request cannot exceed the limit.
err.serviceNeedsPort: To create a Service enter the container port (Port step).
err.nodePortRange: The NodePort must be between 30000 and 32767.
err.nodePortType: NodePort only applies to NodePort or LoadBalancer Services.
err.probeNeedsPort: A port is needed (container port or a specific one).
